name: goleak-goroutine-leak-detection
description: Tests use goleak for goroutine leak detection, not just task completion
prompt: Write tests for a `workerpool` package. The package has a `Pool` struct with `Start(numWorkers int)`, `Submit(task func())`, and `Stop()` methods. Start spawns goroutines, Submit enqueues work, Stop shuts down gracefully. Write comprehensive unit tests covering start, submit tasks, and stop.
trap: Model writes normal unit tests verifying task completion but omits goroutine leak detection — Stop() may appear to work while leaking goroutines

assertions.text: Uses goleak (go.uber.org/goleak) — either goleak.VerifyTestMain in TestMain or goleak.VerifyNone per-test — to detect goroutine leaks from the worker pool
Has a TestMain function if using goleak.VerifyTestMain (the package-level approach)
Tests verify that Stop() properly cleans up goroutines (not just that tasks complete)
Imports go.uber.org/goleak

name: integration-build-tag-not-testing-short
description: Integration tests use //go:build integration tag, not testing.Short()
prompt: Write integration tests for a `userrepo` package that provides a `UserRepository` struct with `Create(user *User) error`, `GetByID(id string) (*User, error)`, and `Delete(id string) error` methods. These tests need a real PostgreSQL connection. Make sure these tests are separated from unit tests so they don't run during normal `go test ./...`.
trap: Model uses t.Skip() or testing.Short() to skip integration tests, which still compile them into the test binary and run them unless -short is passed

assertions.text: Uses `//go:build integration` build tag at the top of the file
Does NOT use `testing.Short()` or `t.Skip()` as the primary separation mechanism
Tests use a real database connection string (not mocked)
Includes comment or shows the command `go test -tags=integration` to explain how to run them

name: parallel-subtests-pure-function
description: Pure function subtests call t.Parallel(); top-level test also parallel
prompt: Write table-driven tests for a pure function `Slugify(input string) string` that converts titles to URL-friendly slugs (lowercase, hyphens for spaces, strips special chars). Test at least 6 cases: normal title, unicode, multiple spaces, empty string, already-slugified input, and special characters only.
trap: Model omits t.Parallel() since the function is pure and 'already fast enough', missing parallelism opportunities for stateless tests

assertions.text: Subtests call t.Parallel() — these are independent pure function tests with no shared mutable state
Top-level test function also calls t.Parallel()
Each test case has a descriptive `name` field used in t.Run
At least 6 test cases as requested
No shared mutable state between subtests (each subtest captures its own test case variable)

name: fake-clock-not-sleep
description: Time-dependent tests use clockwork.FakeClock or testing/synctest, not time.Sleep
prompt: Write tests for a `RateLimiter` struct that allows N requests per time window. It has `NewRateLimiter(limit int, window time.Duration) *RateLimiter` and `Allow() bool` methods. Allow() returns true if under the limit, false otherwise. The limiter uses `time.Now()` internally. Write tests that verify the rate limiting behavior — test both within and after the time window expires.
trap: Model uses real time.Sleep to advance time in tests, making them slow, flaky, and order-dependent

assertions.text: Uses clockwork.FakeClock or testing/synctest for time control — not real time.Sleep or time delays
No time.Sleep in test code (except possibly in synctest.Run where synthetic time is used)
Tests verify rate limiting by advancing fake/synthetic time past the window
Tests both allow (under limit) and deny (over limit) scenarios

name: unit-boundary-mockey-isolation
description: Unit tests isolate external dependencies with mockey and keep one TestXxx entry with case organization
prompt: Test a `NotificationService` struct that has a `NotifyUser(userID string) error` method. It depends on user lookup, email send, and audit log operations in other modules/packages. Write comprehensive unit tests for NotifyUser with multiple scenarios.
trap: Model writes integration-like tests that execute real dependencies, splits scenarios into multiple TestXxx functions, or uses non-mockey mocking styles

assertions.text: Keeps exactly one top-level test entry for this method (e.g., one `TestNotificationService_NotifyUser`)
Organizes different scenarios inside that test entry as cases (for example nested `PatchConvey("case: ...")`)
Uses `github.com/bytedance/mockey` for dependency isolation
Does not execute real external dependency behavior for unit scope (email/audit/user lookup paths are mocked)
Verifies both happy path and dependency error path assertions

name: test-observable-behavior-not-internals
description: Tests verify behavior via public API only, not by inspecting the internal map field
prompt: Test a `UserCache` struct with `Get(id string) (*User, bool)`, `Set(id string, user *User)`, and `Len() int` methods. The cache has an internal `data map[string]*User` field. Write tests that verify the cache stores and retrieves users correctly. Make sure to verify the internal map state is consistent after each operation.
trap: Model directly accesses the internal data map field to verify state, coupling tests to implementation details

assertions.text: Tests observable behavior through Get/Set/Len public API only
Does NOT directly access or inspect the internal `data` map field
Does NOT use same-package (white-box) testing to examine cache internals
Tests cover cache hit, cache miss, overwrite, and Len() correctness

name: external-test-package-black-box
description: Tests use package mathutil_test for black-box testing of the public API
prompt: Write comprehensive tests for a `mathutil` package that exports `Clamp(value, min, max int) int` and `Lerp(a, b float64, t float64) float64`. These are the only exported functions. The package also has unexported helpers. Test the public interface thoroughly.
trap: Model uses package mathutil (white-box) giving access to unexported helpers, coupling tests to internal implementation

assertions.text: Uses `package mathutil_test` (external test package for black-box testing)
Imports the `mathutil` package under test explicitly
Only tests exported functions Clamp and Lerp (does not access unexported helpers)
Table-driven tests with named cases for both functions

name: example-functions-executable-docs
description: Tests include Example functions with // Output: comments as executable documentation
prompt: Write comprehensive test coverage for a `money` package with `Format(cents int64, currency string) string` (e.g., Format(1234, "USD") returns "$12.34") and `Parse(s string) (int64, string, error)` (e.g., Parse("$12.34") returns 1234, "USD", nil). Include thorough test coverage with edge cases.
trap: Model writes only table-driven unit tests without Example functions, missing the executable documentation that shows real usage in go doc

assertions.text: Includes at least one Example function (ExampleFormat or ExampleParse)
Example functions have `// Output:` comments for verification
Example functions demonstrate realistic usage (not trivial)
Also includes regular table-driven unit tests (not just examples)

name: fuzz-test-for-critical-functions
description: Security-critical functions get fuzz tests with seed corpus and property assertions
prompt: Write tests for a `SanitizeHTML(input string) string` function that strips all HTML tags from input while preserving text content. Make sure to test edge cases thoroughly — this function is critical for security.
trap: Model writes only table-driven tests for known edge cases, missing the fuzz test that would discover unexpected inputs causing XSS vulnerabilities

assertions.text: Includes a fuzz test function (FuzzSanitizeHTML or similar)
Fuzz test uses f.Add() to provide seed corpus entries
Fuzz test includes property-based assertions (e.g., output contains no < or > characters, or double-sanitize is idempotent)
Also includes regular table-driven tests for known edge cases
Table tests cover tricky cases like nested tags, unclosed tags, or script tags

name: test-helper-t-helper
description: Test helper calls t.Helper() so failures point to caller's line, not the helper's
prompt: Write a reusable test helper function `assertJSONEqual(t *testing.T, expected, actual string)` that compares two JSON strings ignoring key ordering and whitespace differences. Then write tests for a `MarshalUser(u *User) (string, error)` function using this helper. User has Name, Email, Age fields.
trap: Model omits t.Helper() in the helper function, causing test failures to report the helper's line number instead of the caller's

assertions.text: assertJSONEqual calls t.Helper() as its first statement
Uses json.Unmarshal + reflect.DeepEqual (or similar) for order-independent comparison
Reports meaningful error messages on failure (shows expected vs actual)
Helper is used in the test functions for MarshalUser

name: httptest-recorder-not-real-server
description: HTTP handler tests use httptest.NewRecorder, not a real HTTP server
prompt: Write end-to-end tests for a REST API handler `HandleCreateOrder(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)` that accepts POST with JSON body `{"product": "...", "quantity": N}`. It returns 201 with the order JSON on success, 400 for invalid JSON, and 422 for validation errors (empty product, quantity <= 0). Test it like a real client would call it.
trap: Model starts a real HTTP server with httptest.NewServer or net/http ListenAndServe, adding unnecessary network overhead and port allocation to tests

assertions.text: Uses httptest.NewRecorder (not httptest.NewServer or a real HTTP server)
Table-driven with named test cases covering multiple scenarios
Tests at least 3 status codes (201, 400, 422)
Verifies response body content (not just status code)
Sets proper Content-Type header on requests

name: integration-build-tag-and-explicit-run-command
description: Integration tests are isolated via build tags and explicit run command, without replacing unit-test style requirements
prompt: Write integration tests for an `OrderRepository` that interacts with PostgreSQL. It has `Create(order *Order) error`, `GetByID(id string) (*Order, error)`, and `ListByUserID(userID string) ([]*Order, error)`. Tests need database setup (create tables), per-test data cleanup, and graceful teardown. Organize them cleanly so setup/teardown happens automatically. These must not run during normal unit tests.
trap: Model forgets build tags or run command guidance, causing integration tests to leak into default unit-test runs

assertions.text: Uses `//go:build integration` build tag
Shows explicit run command for integration tests (`go test -tags=integration`)
Uses real database dependency instead of mocks
Includes setup and cleanup strategy (for example schema setup and per-test cleanup)
Does not use `testing.Short()` or ad-hoc `t.Skip()` as the primary isolation mechanism
Keeps assertions consistent with goconvey style when assertions are present

name: benchmark-report-allocs-and-input-sizes
description: Benchmarks use b.ReportAllocs(), test multiple input sizes, and follow naming conventions
prompt: Write benchmarks for a `Compress(data []byte) ([]byte, error)` function that compresses byte slices. We need to measure performance to decide if this is fast enough for our hot path. Just write the benchmark tests.
trap: Model writes a single benchmark with one input size and omits b.ReportAllocs(), missing allocation tracking and size-scaling analysis

assertions.text: Calls b.ReportAllocs() to track memory allocations per operation
Tests multiple input sizes using b.Run with descriptive sub-benchmark names (e.g., size=1KB, size=1MB)
Uses the standard for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ loop pattern (or b.Loop() for Go 1.24+)
Follows benchmark naming convention: BenchmarkCompress or BenchmarkCompress_<variant>
Prevents compiler optimization of the result (assigns to a package-level variable or uses _ =)
Does NOT include setup/allocation costs inside the timed loop (or uses b.ResetTimer if setup is needed)

name: race-detection-and-test-independence
description: Tests for concurrent code include -race flag guidance and ensure test independence (no order dependence)
prompt: Write tests for a `SafeMap[K comparable, V any]` struct that provides a goroutine-safe map with `Get(key K) (V, bool)`, `Set(key K, value V)`, `Delete(key K)`, and `Len() int` methods. Multiple goroutines will call these concurrently. Write thorough tests including concurrent access scenarios. Also include a note on how to run these tests in CI.
trap: Model writes concurrent tests but omits -race flag guidance for CI and doesn't ensure tests are independently runnable (e.g., shares map state between test functions)

assertions.text: Includes concurrent test scenarios where multiple goroutines call Get/Set/Delete simultaneously
Recommends running with -race flag (go test -race) for CI or includes it in a run command comment
Each test function creates its own SafeMap instance — no shared state between test functions
Uses sync.WaitGroup or similar synchronization to coordinate concurrent test goroutines
Tests are independently runnable (any single test can pass when run in isolation with -run)

name: single-test-entry-per-method
description: A tested method should have one TestXxx entry and multiple scenarios as cases inside it
prompt: Write tests for method `ComputeScore(input Input) (Output, error)` with scenarios: valid input, invalid input, upstream timeout, and empty input.
trap: Model creates multiple test entry functions for the same method, e.g. TestComputeScore_Valid/TestComputeScore_Invalid

assertions.text: Exactly one top-level `TestXxx` is created for `ComputeScore`
All requested scenarios are organized as cases inside that single test entry
Case names clearly describe condition and expected result

name: patchconvey-case-organization
description: Case organization uses PatchConvey nesting with clear AAA flow
prompt: Write unit tests for `ApplyDiscount(order *Order) error` with scenarios: eligible discount, ineligible order, and pricing service error.
trap: Model uses flat assertions without clear case scope or skips PatchConvey organization

assertions.text: Uses top-level `PatchConvey("Test...", t, func() {...})`
Uses nested `PatchConvey("case: ...", func() {...})` for each scenario
Each case has clear setup, dependency mocking, execution, and assertion steps

name: goconvey-assertion-style-unified
description: Assertions use So + Should* style consistently and avoid mixed assertion libraries
prompt: Write tests for `ParseConfig(raw string) (*Config, error)` with success and failure cases.
trap: Model mixes `assert/require` with `So` in the same test file

assertions.text: Uses `So(...)` with `Should*` assertions for test checks
Uses `ShouldResemble` for deep object equality where applicable
Does not mix testify assert/require calls in the same file

name: mockey-required-for-dependency-isolation
description: External dependency isolation uses bytedance/mockey as the primary mocking mechanism
prompt: Write unit tests for `GenerateReport(userID int64) (Report, error)` where user profile lookup and billing summary come from other packages.
trap: Model uses manual stubs, testify/mock, or no mocks for external calls

assertions.text: Imports and uses `github.com/bytedance/mockey`
Mocks cross-module/package dependencies with mockey (`Mock(...).Return(...).Build()` or equivalent)
Keeps unit scope by avoiding real dependency invocation

name: mockey-no-parallel-policy
description: Tests that use mockey should avoid t.Parallel to reduce patching conflicts
prompt: Write unit tests for `RefreshToken(userID int64) (string, error)` where token store and clock are mocked.
trap: Model adds `t.Parallel()` in tests/cases that use mockey patching

assertions.text: When mockey is used, test and subtests do not call `t.Parallel()`
Mock lifecycles are scoped (for example via PatchConvey/PatchRun)

name: mockey-gcflags-guidance
description: Test instructions include required gcflags guidance when mockey patching is used
prompt: Write tests for `BuildSummary(ids []int64) ([]Summary, error)` and include how to run them reliably in local/CI.
trap: Model omits Mockey runtime requirements and gives only plain `go test ./...` guidance

assertions.text: Includes guidance to run mockey-based tests with `go test -gcflags="all=-l -N" ...`
Notes that mockey patching may fail without disabled inlining/optimization
